# White Leaf Technology Group

> White Leaf Technology Group identifies emerging technologies, and existing technology used in non-dairy applications, that can be applied in the dairy industry. The goal is a safer and healthier environment for dairy animals. Products need to offer a measurable return on investment to the dairy farm of 1 year or less. The first product technology being released is LED technology consisting of germicidal and therapy lighting: red and blue light therapy and disinfection fixtures for dairy barns. Videos on the site are artistic renderings.

The blue light is continuous low-level violet-blue light in a selected band of the visible spectrum.

## Applications

Case studies will be available shortly.

- [Milking Holsteins](https://www.whiteleafled.com/#app-milking-holsteins): LED light therapy and disinfection technology is installed in fixtures over the cow stalls in the free stall building. In head-to-head stalls, one large fixture covers a total of 10 cows. A smaller fixture with directional technology covers 5 cows along wall stalls. Farmers, herd masters, and farm nutritionists have confirmed an average increase in milk production of 4.5–6.5 lbs more per cow under the lights. On one test farm, 2nd and 3rd year lactation cows under the lights were tracked against 2nd and 3rd lactation cows on the other side of the main feed aisle under standard lighting. That comparison showed 4.5 lbs more milk per cow for the group under the LED light therapy and disinfection fixtures. All groups were fed from the same mixer at the same time each day. Multiple dairy farms installed and tracked the data over a period of 6+ years.

- [Calving pen](https://www.whiteleafled.com/#app-nursery): LED therapy and disinfection fixtures are used in the free stall building, nursery area. Red light heals and repairs tissue, reduces pain and inflammation, improves joint and muscle health, and increases blood circulation. Blue light will improve barn hygiene / air quality around the cows, reduces heavy load of bacteria on the cow, and reducing subclinical infections.

- [Heifer Huts](https://www.whiteleafled.com/#app-heifer-huts): Red wavelengths penetrate directly through an animal’s skin and eyes, transform into cellular energy, and kick-start metabolic events, including stimulation of collagen production and an increase in ATP. Red light helps develop the newborn heifer immune system, helps fight off bacterial or viral infections, improves joint and muscle health, and increases blood circulation. Blue light is deadly for bacteria but safe for continuous exposure and harmless to humans and animals. It helps sanitize all feeding equipment; continuous sanitization of the calf hut keeps bacterial counts low.

- [Water Troughs](https://www.whiteleafled.com/#app-water-troughs): White Leaf’s all-blue linear fixture uses patented viewing optics that direct 95% of the light into the trough / water. It helps kill harmful bacteria in the cow water troughs. With continuous sanitization, the water in the trough keeps bacterial counts low. Blue light is deadly for bacteria but safe for continuous exposure and harmless to humans and animals.

- [How we kill the Unseen Enemy](https://www.whiteleafled.com/#app-how-we-kill-unseen-enemy): Applications video.

- [How Heavy Loads of Bacteria Impact a Milking Cow](https://www.whiteleafled.com/#app-bacteria-impact-milking-cow): Several key bacteria threaten dairy farm milking operations, causing udder infections, milk quality degradation, and animal health risks. Mastitis is the most costly disease in dairy farming, damaging udder tissue and reducing milk yield. The page names Staphylococcus aureus (contagious), Streptococcus agalactiae (contagious), Escherichia coli (environmental), Streptococcus uberis (environmental), Streptococcus dysgalactiae (environmental/contagious), and Klebsiella (environmental), with the roles given on that page. Fighting off bacteria takes an immense amount of energy from a milking cow, particularly in the form of glucose. An acute immune response can consume over 1 kilogram (2.2 lbs) of pure glucose every 12 hours. A major bacterial challenge can cause a sudden drop in milk production of 20 to 40 pounds or more per day because the energy is diverted away from the udder.

- [Whey Material](https://www.whiteleafled.com/#app-unseen-enemy): Applications video.

## How it works

[How it works](https://www.whiteleafled.com/#technology)

Light emitting diodes (LEDs) are semiconductors that convert electrical energy into light energy. The color of the light depends on the semiconductor material, and each color does a different job. LEDs are generally classified into ultraviolet, visible, and infrared. White Leaf’s red and blue LED fixtures sit in the visible band, each at its own wavelength and frequency. The blue light is continuous low-level violet-blue light in a selected band of the visible spectrum.

Frequency is how many wave cycles pass a point each second. Wavelength is the distance from one crest to the next. Higher frequencies have shorter wavelengths. Lower frequencies have longer wavelengths. Visible light is a narrow band between ultraviolet and infrared.

Red light:

- Penetrates directly through an animal’s skin and eyes.
- Transforms into cellular energy, kick-starting metabolic events, including stimulation of collagen production and an increase in ATP, a boost of energy to the cells.
- Heals and repairs tissue.
- Reduces pain and inflammation.
- Improves joint and muscle health.
- Increases blood circulation.

Blue light:

- Blue light LED technology has no harmful side effects. It is safe for continuous exposure and harmless to humans and animals.
- Laboratory and clinical studies have validated its killing power over a range of pathogenic bacteria, including Staphylococcus aureus, MRSA, coagulase-negative Staphylococcus, Streptococcus, Enterococcus, Clostridium, Bacillus, Listeria, Acinetobacter, Pseudomonas, Klebsiella, Proteus, Salmonella, and E. coli.
- Environmental exposure to blue light results in reduction of illnesses and infections contracted through the air or on hard surfaces.

In 1993, Quantum Devices of Barneveld, WI developed a light-emitting diode for NASA to use in its plant growth experiments. A NASA-sponsored research center at the University of Wisconsin-Madison developed Astro culture 3, a plant growth chamber using near infrared HEALS technology for plant growth experiments on shuttle missions. LEDs release energy in the form of photons. Their long wavelengths of light stimulate cells to aid in healing, and NASA went on to study LEDs to increase the metabolism of human cells and stem the loss of bone and muscle in astronauts.
